name: Hungary
tagline: A thermal-water capital on the Danube, a language related to almost nothing, and sweet wine that outlived empires.
summary: Hungary sits on a plain of hot springs — Budapest alone has over a hundred, and the bathing culture runs from Roman to Ottoman to imperial. The language is Finno-Ugric and unrelated to any neighbour, which has shaped a certain separateness. Beyond the capital there is Lake Balaton, the volcanic wine hills above it, and Tokaj, where botrytised wine was made a century before Sauternes.

season.note: Budapest is good year-round and the outdoor thermal baths are best in January, steaming in the cold. Balaton is a summer place and dead outside it. Harvest in Tokaj is October, late.

getting_around: Budapest's metro line 1 is the oldest on the continent after London and still running. Trains reach Balaton, Eger and Tokaj slowly and cheaply. The capital is walkable and its trams are useful.
food: Paprika, in everything, and not interchangeable with chilli
Goulash, which is a soup here and not a stew
Tokaji Aszú, sweet, ancient and unlike any other dessert wine

festivals.name: Sziget Festival, on an island in the Danube

know: The forint, not the euro; exchange rates at street bureaux are usually terrible.
In the baths, bring flip-flops and a towel or hire both; some pools require a cap.
Ruin bars occupy derelict courtyards in the old Jewish quarter, which is also a memorial district — the two coexist awkwardly.

regions.name: Budapest & the Danube Bend
regions.summary: Two cities on either bank, and the river's sharp turn north of them.

cities.name: Budapest
cities.summary: Hilly Buda and flat Pest, joined by bridges, with a parliament on the water and a hundred hot springs underneath.
highlights: Széchenyi and Gellért baths — one grand and outdoor, one Art Nouveau and indoor
The parliament, seen from the Buda side at night
The Great Market Hall, and lángos on the upper floor
The House of Terror, in the building both secret polices used

experiences.name: An outdoor thermal bath in winter
experiences.summary: 38°C water, snow on the stone, and old men playing chess on floating boards. Go early; go on a weekday.

experiences.name: A ruin bar, before it fills
experiences.summary: Derelict courtyard buildings filled with salvaged furniture; Szimpla was the first and is still worth an early evening.

cities.name: Szentendre
cities.summary: A Serbian Orthodox artists' town on the river, forty minutes from the capital by suburban rail.
highlights: Orthodox churches from the 18th-century Serb migration
The open-air ethnographic museum outside town
Marzipan, oddly, and a museum of it

regions.name: Balaton & the Wine Country
regions.summary: Central Europe's largest lake, volcanic hills above it, and Tokaj to the northeast.

cities.name: Tihany, Lake Balaton
cities.summary: A lavender peninsula with an abbey on a cliff, sticking into a shallow warm lake.
highlights: The abbey and its 1055 founding charter — the oldest written Hungarian
Water warm enough to stand in for hours, and rarely deeper than four metres

cities.name: Tokaj
cities.summary: The world's first classified wine region, from 1737, on volcanic slopes at a river confluence.
highlights: Aszú berries picked individually, one shrivelled grape at a time
Cellars cut into rock and furred with black mould
Dry furmint, which is the region's current argument

experiences.name: A mouldy cellar in Tokaj
experiences.summary: The black fungus on the walls regulates humidity and is left alone deliberately; taste dry furmint first and six-puttonyos last.
